finding: All 81 component directories include index.ts, a primary .ts file, a .styles.ts file, a .stories.ts file, and a .test.ts file. One exception: hx-style-scope keeps its test in __tests__/hx-style-scope.test.ts, which is a valid alternative location and is exercised by the test runner.
All components use the hx- tag prefix, --hx- CSS custom property prefix, and hx- event prefix consistently across all 81 component directories. No naming violations found.
No 'any' types, no @ts-ignore or @ts-expect-error annotations, and no non-null assertions found across all component source files. TypeScript strict mode is honored uniformly.
All lifecycle methods (updated, willUpdate, firstUpdated) that accept changed properties correctly use PropertyValues<this> as the parameter type, satisfying the Lit strict typing requirement.
All CustomEvent dispatches verified to include both bubbles: true and composed: true. The grep false-positive was a context issue; all event constructors inspected include correct options.
All 81 component classes include @tag, @summary, @slot, @fires (where events are dispatched), @csspart, and @cssprop JSDoc annotations. CEM documentation is uniformly present.

hx-prose.styles.ts imports raw CSS via '../../styles/prose/prose.scoped.css?raw' using a Vite-specific query suffix and no .js extension. The file exports raw CSS string, not a Lit CSSResult, which is architecturally distinct but intentional for adopted stylesheets. The import path pattern is non-standard relative to other components.
recommendation: Document in a component-level comment that this file intentionally uses ?raw import for AdoptedStylesheetsController and does not follow the standard Lit css`` template pattern. No :host display rule is needed or expected since hx-prose renders in Light DOM via createRenderRoot returning this.

finding: hx-form.styles.ts imports raw CSS via '../../styles/form/form.scoped.css?raw' without .js extension, same pattern as hx-prose. The missing :host display rule is expected since hx-form is a Light DOM component using createRenderRoot returning this.
recommendation: Document in a comment that this file uses ?raw import intentionally for AdoptedStylesheetsController. The non-.js extension is acceptable for CSS raw imports. Add a note explaining why no :host display rule is present.

finding: hx-number-input.styles.ts uses many primitive design tokens (--hx-space-1, --hx-font-size-sm, --hx-font-weight-medium, etc.) without hardcoded fallback values, unlike hx-button and hx-text-input which consistently provide fallbacks (e.g., var(--hx-space-1, 0.25rem)). This makes the component fail silently if the token package is not loaded.
recommendation: Add hardcoded fallback values to all primitive token references in hx-number-input.styles.ts, matching the pattern used in hx-button.styles.ts and hx-text-input.styles.ts: e.g., gap: var(--hx-space-1, 0.25rem); font-size: var(--hx-font-size-sm, 0.875rem);

finding: hx-number-input.styles.ts uses :focus:not(:focus-visible) to suppress the focus ring for mouse/touch, which is the correct pattern. However, the checklist rule is :focus-visible only (never bare :focus). The usage here is intentional and correct — the :focus selector is only used to suppress styles, not apply them.
recommendation: Add an inline comment clarifying this is the standard mouse-focus suppression pattern to prevent future reviewers from flagging it as a violation: /* suppress outline for pointer focus; :focus-visible handles keyboard/programmatic focus */

finding: hx-menu.styles.ts uses hardcoded rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1) values as the fallback for --hx-menu-shadow. These are inside a var(--hx-menu-shadow, <fallback>) expression so they function as the CSS custom property fallback, not a hardcoded value. The pattern is acceptable but a design token for the shadow (--hx-shadow-md) would be preferable.
recommendation: Replace the hardcoded rgb() fallback shadow with a reference to a shared shadow token: box-shadow: var(--hx-menu-shadow, var(--hx-shadow-md, 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)));

finding: hx-toast.styles.ts uses hardcoded rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1) values as the fallback for --hx-toast-shadow. Same pattern as hx-menu — inside a CSS custom property fallback, acceptable but suboptimal. hx-nav also exhibits this same pattern.
recommendation: Use var(--hx-shadow-md) as the intermediate token: box-shadow: var(--hx-toast-shadow, var(--hx-shadow-md, 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), ...));

finding: hx-nav.styles.ts uses hardcoded rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1) shadow values as fallback for --hx-shadow-md directly (at least uses the semantic token name). This is slightly better than hx-menu and hx-toast.
recommendation: No change required as --hx-shadow-md is the semantic token and the hardcoded fallback is correct. Consistent with token architecture.

finding: hx-side-nav.styles.ts uses hardcoded rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1) for a hover state background. There is a comment indicating it is a fallback for browsers without color-mix(). The intent is correct but the CSS custom property reference (--hx-overlay-white-10) is non-standard and may not be defined in the token package.
recommendation: Verify --hx-overlay-white-10 is defined in the hx-tokens package. If not, either add it or use color-mix(in srgb, white 10%, transparent) as the primary value with the rgba fallback inside a @supports block.

finding: hx-spinner.styles.ts uses rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3) as an explicit fallback for browsers without color-mix() support, inside a var(--hx-overlay-white-30, rgba(...)) expression. The comment documents the browser compatibility reason. Pattern is acceptable.

hx-icon.ts uses unsafeHTML for rendering fetched SVG content, which is the only viable approach for inline SVG rendering. A thorough _sanitizeSvg() method strips script elements, foreignObject nodes, on* event handlers, style attributes, and javascript:/data: URIs from URL-bearing attributes before rendering. The usage is properly justified and the sanitization is comprehensive.

hx-phi-field correctly uses @property({ attribute: false }) for the 'data' property to prevent PHI from being written to the DOM as an HTML attribute. A devWarn fires if a consumer attempts to set it via attribute. HIPAA-compliant implementation.

hx-dropdown extends LitElement directly instead of HelixElement. This is consistent with the majority of components in the library (60+ of 81 components still use LitElement). The HelixElement migration is incomplete across the library.
recommendation: Migrate hx-dropdown to extend HelixElement as part of the broader HelixElement migration effort. This is a systemic issue affecting the majority of components, not an isolated defect.

finding: 60 of 81 component classes extend LitElement directly instead of HelixElement. HelixElement provides lazy ElementInternals access, form lifecycle hook delegation, and eliminates constructor boilerplate for form-associated components. Only 21 components (hx-button, hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-checkbox, hx-radio-group, hx-switch, hx-slider, hx-toggle-button, hx-number-input, hx-date-picker, hx-time-picker, hx-file-upload, hx-icon-button, hx-textarea, hx-combobox, hx-color-picker, hx-rating, hx-code-snippet, hx-clinical-status, hx-checkbox-group, hx-style-scope) have been migrated.
recommendation: Systematically migrate remaining 60 LitElement components to extend HelixElement. The migration is mechanical: replace 'extends LitElement' with 'extends HelixElement' and update the import. Non-form components require no other changes. Prioritize in order of complexity: layout components (hx-stack, hx-grid, hx-container) first, interactive components (hx-dropdown, hx-nav, hx-menu) second.

finding: hx-accordion.test.ts is 1255 lines and covers rendering, properties, keyboard navigation, accordion-item sub-component, and accessibility. Comprehensive for a compound component.
hx-button.test.ts is 903 lines covering all 6 variants, 3 sizes, disabled state, loading state, anchor rendering, form association, events, slots, and axe-core accessibility. Excellent coverage.

hx-divider.test.ts is 214 lines — the smallest test file — but the component is simple (2 properties: orientation, spacing; 1 slot; decorative mode). Coverage is proportionate: rendering, orientation, spacing, label slot, decorative mode, and 5 axe-core checks all present.
hx-visually-hidden.test.ts is 229 lines. The component has minimal surface area (content slotting + CSS only). Coverage is proportionate.
hx-date-picker.test.ts is 1468 lines — one of the most thoroughly tested components. Form association, keyboard navigation, locale, and accessibility are all covered.
hx-time-picker.test.ts is 1481 lines — the largest test file, appropriate for a complex form component with time validation, AM/PM handling, and keyboard navigation.

hx-menu.test.ts covers hx-menu and hx-menu-item but does not include a dedicated test describe block for hx-menu-divider. The hx-menu-divider is a separate registered custom element with its own role=separator and aria semantics.
recommendation: Add a describe('hx-menu-divider') block to hx-menu.test.ts that tests: renders with shadow DOM, exposes 'base' CSS part, has role='separator', has aria-orientation='horizontal', and no axe-core violations.

finding: hx-side-nav.test.ts covers hx-side-nav and uses hx-nav-item in fixtures, but does not have an isolated describe block for hx-nav-item as a standalone component. hx-nav-item is a separate registered custom element with its own properties (href, active, disabled, expanded) and stories file.
recommendation: Add a describe('hx-nav-item') block to hx-side-nav.test.ts covering its standalone properties, CSS parts, aria attributes, and disabled state, similar to how hx-accordion-item is tested within hx-accordion.test.ts.

finding: hx-table.test.ts imports all 6 sub-component types and tests them through composition. There are no isolated describe blocks for hx-tbody, hx-thead, hx-tfoot, hx-tr, hx-th, or hx-td as standalone components. hx-th in particular has sorting functionality and a custom hx-sort event that merits direct testing.
recommendation: Add isolated describe blocks for hx-th (sort event, aria-sort, disabled sort) and hx-td (colspan, alignment) as standalone components within the hx-table.test.ts file.

finding: hx-toast.test.ts covers hx-toast, hx-toast-stack, and the toast-factory imperative API. All three public surfaces are tested.
hx-color-picker.test.ts is 1020 lines and includes inline tests of the color-utils.ts utility functions (hexToRgb, etc.) as part of the component test file. Color conversion edge cases are tested.

hx-style-scope test is located in __tests__/hx-style-scope.test.ts (non-standard location) rather than the sibling hx-style-scope.test.ts convention. The test file itself is thorough. The __tests__ directory location is a structural inconsistency but does not affect correctness.
recommendation: Consider moving __tests__/hx-style-scope.test.ts to the sibling hx-style-scope.test.ts location to match the convention of all other 80 components. Update any import path references accordingly.

finding: All 81 component story files include play() functions with interaction tests. Not a single component lacks interactive story tests. This is excellent — Storybook interaction coverage is complete across the entire library.

hx-dropdown has only 8 stories for a component that supports 8 placement variants, disabled state, custom triggers, and keyboard navigation. The KeyboardNavigation story exists but placement variants are collapsed into a single Placements story without individual named exports for each placement position.
recommendation: Add individual story exports for each of the 8 placement variants (top, top-start, top-end, bottom, bottom-start, bottom-end, start, end) so each can be visually tested and screenshot independently during VRT runs.

finding: hx-counter has only 7 stories. The component supports multiple easing variants and animation behaviors. The EasingVariants story exists but does not have an individual story per easing type, making it harder to catch regressions on specific variants.
recommendation: Add individual story exports for each easing variant (linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out) to support per-variant visual regression testing.

finding: hx-help-text has 7 stories. The component is simple (text only, error state, disabled state) and 7 stories is adequate for its surface area.
hx-visually-hidden has 6 stories. The component is a utility with minimal visual surface. Story count is proportionate.
hx-style-scope has 6 stories. The component is an infrastructure utility (adopted stylesheets scoping) with limited visual variants. Story count is proportionate to its use case.

hx-patient-banner correctly implements the Joint Commission NPSG.01.01.01 two-identifier rule via the enforce-identifier-rule property, dispatches hx-identifier-rule-violation with full detail, and integrates with hx-phi-field for HIPAA-compliant PHI display. CEM documentation is thorough and healthcare-domain-specific.
All animated components (hx-spinner, hx-skeleton, hx-progress-bar, hx-carousel, hx-toast) implement @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) correctly. No animation runs without user preference check.
No uses of eval(), Function() constructor, inline event handlers in templates, or unguarded user content rendering found across all 81 component source files. Security posture is clean.
No orphaned imports, dead code blocks, or commented-out code found. Inline comments with P1-/P2- prefixes are code audit reference markers documenting deliberate decisions, not dead code or hacks.

hx-action-bar.styles.ts has no :host([disabled]) CSS rule, despite the component checking for disabled state on child elements in its JavaScript logic. hx-action-bar delegates disabled to children rather than hosting it as a direct property, but this should be documented explicitly.
recommendation: Either add a comment in hx-action-bar.styles.ts explaining why :host([disabled]) is absent (disabled is delegated to child elements, not the host), or add :host([disabled]) styling with pointer-events: none and opacity for consistency with other components that participate in disabled group patterns.

finding: HTMLElementTagNameMap declarations are present in all 81 component main source files, enabling TypeScript autocomplete and type safety for document.querySelector and DOM API consumers.

hx-format-date includes a DRUPAL.md file documenting the FOUC tradeoff and SEO implications of client-side date formatting in a Drupal context. This is excellent consumer-facing documentation for a healthcare CMS integration pattern.

hx-prose correctly uses createRenderRoot returning 'this' for Light DOM rendering, which is necessary for CKEditor/CMS rich text content to receive global styles. The AdoptedStylesheetsController pattern is correct for avoiding style duplication.

hx-form correctly uses Light DOM (createRenderRoot returning this) for native form participation and Drupal compatibility. The no-action pattern for Drupal (renders only a slot) is well-documented in JSDoc.

hx-menu-divider is a standalone registered custom element (hx-menu-divider tag) with its own role=separator and aria-orientation=horizontal. It has no dedicated test coverage — neither in hx-menu.test.ts nor in a separate file. Its accessibility semantics are untested.
recommendation: Add at minimum 4 tests to hx-menu.test.ts in a describe('hx-menu-divider') block: renders with shadow DOM, exposes 'base' CSS part, sets role='separator', sets aria-orientation='horizontal', and passes axe-core.

finding: hx-radio-group.test.ts (876 lines) and hx-radio.test.ts (separate file) both exist and provide thorough coverage of the compound component including ARIA group semantics, individual radio button keyboard navigation, and form association.
